routing.source: Why I Hate (and Why I Love) the Wizard.md
routing.observation: Heightened spells naturally fall behind native-rank spells — this is the design tension the Rudimental Perfectionism thesis addresses.

routing.source: Why I Hate (and Why I Love) the Wizard.md
routing.observation: Force spells could be converted via the exploit trait into a mini-blast with forced movement when their intended use case doesn't come up.

routing.source: Witch and Wizard Blaster Build Guides.md
routing.observation: Sustain spells are fundamentally good for three-slot casters — they let you get repeated value from a single spell slot. Sustain spells can be cast one rank below max and still be very good because repeated damage over multiple rounds compensates for the slightly lower per-hit numbers.

routing.source: Witch and Wizard Blaster Build Guides.md
routing.observation: Multimodal spells are more valuable on prepared casters — spells that are good in multiple situations reduce the pain of 'I prepared the wrong thing today.'
routing.reason: No multimodal field in spell-data.js

routing.source: Witch and Wizard Blaster Build Guides.md
routing.observation: Arcane is the better blasting tradition than Primal for two reasons: Will-targeting blasts become available from rank 3 onward, whereas Primal's Will-targeting options lean debuff rather than blast, and Shore Strike and Force Barrage provide a reliability floor that Primal lacks entirely.

routing.source: Witch and Wizard Blaster Build Guides.md
routing.observation: Three categories of spells to feed your low-rank slots: Silver bullets (Acid Grip, Earthbind), Reactions you'd cast between turns (Hidebound, Brine Dragon's Bile), Campaign-relevant utility.
routing.reason: "silverBullets" is not a role value in spell-data.js

routing.source: Witch and Wizard Blaster Build Guides.md
routing.observation: Reactions are good options for low-rank slots since you'd cast them between turns.

routing.source: Witch and Wizard Blaster Build Guides.md
routing.observation: Arcane casters get Will-targeting blasts from rank 3 onward (Agonizing Despair, Vision of Death, Phantasmal Calamity, Phantasmagoria), whereas Primal's Will-targeting options lean debuff rather than blast.
routing.reason: General spell selection philosophy, not per-spell applicable

routing.source: Theoretical vs Practical Utility Spells.md
routing.observation: Buying heuristic: scroll for once-per-adventure needs, wand for once-per-day needs. Consumable utility costs zero combat prowess.

routing.source: Theoretical vs Practical Utility Spells.md
routing.observation: Past ~level 7, surplus low-rank slots make slot-cast utility nearly free — skipping it leaves power on the table.

routing.source: Theoretical vs Practical Utility Spells.md
routing.observation: PF2e utility is weaker spell-for-spell than D&D's but sees more table play — opportunity cost, not raw power, drives actual usage.
